item.title: EDITORIAL: Pass rational tax reform for relief
item.description: Inflation and wage stagnation have combined to make staying afloat a struggle for households in the middle, nationwide. Here in Hawaii, it’s worse: The cost of living hits households with average incomes at all the pain points, including groceries, energy and especially housing.

item.title: Finance Department warns public of DMV phishing text scam
item.description: LIHUE — The Finance Department is warning the public about continued phishing scams involving fraudulent text messages that falsely claim to be from the Hawaii Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

item.title: ‘Lovable’ 4-year-old named Children’s Miracle Network Champion
item.description: HONOLULU — Seeley Borges of Kauai was named Hawaii’s 2026 Children’s Miracle Network Champion, announced the Kapiolani Medical Center for Women and Children on Thursday.

item.title: Gay & Robinson, Inc. to host annual wildfire preparedness community meetings for tenants
item.description: KAUMAKANI — Gay & Robinson, Inc. will conduct its first annual wildfire preparedness outreach and education for tenants through two Community Meetings: March 30 at 5:30 p.m. and March 31 at 8:30 a.m.

item.title: Officials urge residents to take storm seriously as deluge reaches state
item.description: The storm system hitting Hawaii this week could bring up to 30 inches of rain to parts of Oahu through the weekend, and city officials have one key message for residents: stay home.

item.title: DOW provides tips for severe weather preparation
item.description: LIHUE — The Department of Water (DOW) reminds residents to follow water emergency preparedness guidelines and to stay informed about water service advisories that may be issued during emergencies.

item.title: More bad weather coming
item.description: LIHUE — At the wettest point of the overnight Kona Low storm on Kauai, the National Weather Service (NWS) reported that nearly 7 inches of rain — 6.90 inches at the North Wailua recording station — fell in a hydrologic report ending at 5 a.m. Wednesday.

item.title: County issues safety advisory ahead of storm
item.description: LIHUE — County of Kauai officials are urging the public to be vigilant due to severe weather conditions.

item.title: Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami’s State of the County
item.description: Good morning and thank you for not joining us for our eighth and final State of the County address. As you can probably hear outside, mother nature had other plans for us today. In true Kaua‘i fashion, she showed up, settled in, and made herself quite comfortable.
